Enslaved as a young Orthodox Christian, this close friend of Suleiman the Magnificent became the Ottoman Empire's first grand vizier in 1523 before being executed on the sultan's orders in 1536 — who was he?

Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire from 1523 to 1536. Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha (c. 1495 – 15 March 1536), was the first grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire appointed by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

Governing France during the childhood of Louis XV, whom he was related to as both great-nephew and first cousin twice removed, this early 18th-century regent married a daughter of Louis XIV — who is he?
Philippe II, Duke of Orléans: Regent of France from 1715 to 1723.
What single word names the practice of banning by law the making, selling, and drinking of alcoholic beverages?

Rooted in a Greek word meaning 'to snatch away' from First Thessalonians, this end-times evangelical belief holds that living and dead Christians alike will rise to meet Christ in the clouds — what is it called?
This three-time Conservative prime minister, who doubled as Foreign Secretary for most of his tenure, championed a foreign policy he called 'splendid isolation' — who was he?
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood
Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury: British prime minister (1885-86; 1886-92; 1895-1902)
This Emir led Kuwait from 2006 until his death in 2020, having been the fourth son of a previous ruling sheikh — who was he?
Sabah Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah: Emir of Kuwait from 2006 to 2020.

His 1971 book "Rules for Radicals: A Pragmatic Primer" defended both confrontation and compromise, drawn from his work with Chicago's Industrial Areas Foundation organizing poor communities — which American activist wrote it?
Saul Alinsky: American activist and political theorist (1909–1972)
This Indian politician served four terms as Chief Minister of Maharashtra and founded a new party in 1999 after splitting from the Indian National Congress — who is he?
Sharad Pawar: Indian politician. Sharadchandra Govindrao Pawar (born 12 December 1940) is an Indian politician who has served as a Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha since 2014.

In just 96 hours of 1967, Israel captured the West Bank, Gaza, the Sinai Peninsula, and the Golan Heights from three Arab nations—a lightning campaign that reshaped the Middle East. What is this brief but transformative war called?
Six-Day War: 1967 war between Israel and Arab states.
Released from Dutch detention by invading Japanese forces in WWII, this nationalist leader went on to become the very first president of his newly independent nation. Who is he?
Sukarno: President of Indonesia from 1945 to 1967.
This brief conflict ran from June 27 to July 7, 1991, ending when the Brioni Accords settled Slovenia's break from Yugoslavia — what was it called?

Ten-Day War: 1991 Slovenia-Yugoslavia conflict. It was fought between the Slovenian Territorial Defence and the Slovenian National Police Force on one side, and the Yugoslav People's Army on the other.
Before ruling Rome from 79 to 81 AD, he commanded the siege that ended the Jewish rebellion — and became the first Roman emperor ever to directly succeed his own biological father; who was he?
Titus: Roman emperor from AD 79 to 81. Titus Flavius Vespasianus (30 December 39 – 13 September 81 AD) was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD.
Explicitly authorized by the Constitution, this independent government agency replaced a Cabinet department in 1971 and holds a legal monopoly on traditional letter delivery — which agency?
United States Postal Service: Independent agency of the U.S. federal government.

His brother was executed for revolutionary activities in 1887, pushing him toward radical politics. He founded the Bolsheviks, led the October Revolution, and created the world's first communist state—then ruled it until his death in 1924. Who was this Russian revolutionary?
Vladimir Lenin: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1924.
Introduced to the public in 1954 by a retired British civil servant, this modern pagan, Earth-focused religion blends ancient motifs with 20th-century hermetic ideas — which religion?
Wicca: Modern syncretic pagan religion. Wicca draws upon ancient pagan and 20th-century hermetic motifs for theological and ritual purposes.
This 7th-century Chinese Buddhist monk journeyed to the Indian subcontinent from 629 to 645 CE and brought back more than 650 Sanskrit texts to translate — who is he?
Xuanzang: Chinese Buddhist monk and scholar (602–664)
Born into poverty and adopted by a wealthy uncle, this Chinese general commanded the Eighth Route Army and is regarded as a principal founder of the People's Republic. Who was he?
Zhu De: Chinese general and politician (1886–1976)
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Ma Jun (mechanical engineer) (born 200) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Jīvaka (born 401 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Giordano Bruno is an astronomer. Bruno's pantheism was not taken lightly by the church, nor was his teaching of metempsychosis regarding the reincarnation of the soul.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Roger Penrose is a mathematician. Sir Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.
What is the atomic number of Cadmium?
Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
What is the atomic number of Lead?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.
In what year was John von Neumann born?
John von Neumann: During World War II, von Neumann worked on the Manhattan Project.
In what year was Manmohan Singh born?
Manmohan Singh: A member of the Indian National Congress, Singh was the first and remains the only Sikh prime minister of India.
In what year was Paracelsus born?
Paracelsus also had a substantial influence as a prophet or diviner, his "Prognostications" being studied by Rosicrucians in the 17th century.
In what year did B. R. Ambedkar die?
B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
In which country is Kazan phenomenon?
Kazan phenomenon: Soviet Union. The Kazan mafia was known to be particularly cruel in their extortion tactics, and periodically brought in reinforcements from Tatarstan.
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
This tsetse-fly-borne parasitic infection, caused by a protozoan, disproportionately affects humans and cattle across Africa — what is it?
Atrocities in the Congo Free State

African trypanosomiasis is an insect-borne parasitic infection of humans and other animals caused by the protozoan species Trypanosoma brucei, which is transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly.
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI unit measures electric current as one coulomb of charge passing a point per second. What unit is it?
Ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
This severe blood disorder leaves the bone marrow unable to produce enough red cells, white cells, and platelets, often for no known reason — what is it?
Aplastic anemia (AA) is a severe hematologic condition in which the body fails to make blood cells in sufficient numbers.
This 2023 Telugu period action thriller stars Ravi Teja in the title role but became a box-office bomb despite its ambitions. What film is it?
Badger are medium-sized short-legged omnivores in the superfamily Musteloidea.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.
Named in a 2018 New York Times essay by Bari Weiss as part of the 'intellectual dark web,' this former evolutionary biology professor left academia after 2017 campus protests — who is he?
Bret Weinstein (born February 21, 1969) is an American podcaster, author, and former professor of evolutionary biology.
First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, which herbaceous annual takes its specific name from the Latin for 'cultivated' and has long supplied fiber, seed oil, food and medicine?
Cannabis sativa is an annual herbaceous flowering plant.

The scientific study of matter's properties and behavior, this physical science occupies an intermediate position between physics and biology, sometimes called the central science. What is this field of study?
Chemistry is the scientific study of the properties and behavior of matter. Chemistry also addresses the nature of chemical bonds in chemical compounds.
Once a standard topical anesthetic prized for narrowing blood vessels, this tropane alkaloid is extracted from the leaves of South American coca plants — which substance is it?
Cocaine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and tropane alkaloid, derived primarily from the leaves of two coca species native to South America.
Native to North America and smaller than its close relative the gray wolf, this canine fills a similar ecological niche to the golden jackal of Eurasia — which animal?
Coyote (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.

This common cough suppressant found in cold medicine was combined with bupropion in 2022 to create a fast-acting antidepressant, despite belonging to the same chemical class as morphine — what drug is it?
Dextromethorphan is a cough suppressant used in many cough and cold medicines.
Along with the platypus, this quill-covered Australian and New Guinean mammal is one of only two living egg-laying mammal groups, and its young are adorably called puggles — what is it?
Echidna are quill-covered monotremes (egg-laying mammals) belonging to the family Tachyglossidae, living in Australia and New Guinea.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?

Patented in 1979 but not used medically until 1996, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergic rhinitis and hives while causing far less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what's the drug?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Reclassified twice before settling into its own genus, this Gram-variable, non-spore-forming coccobacillus is barely one to 1.5 micrometers across — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.

This American computer scientist and Navy rear admiral devised the theory of machine-independent programming languages and used it to help create COBOL, after being one of the first programmers on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper (ne Murray; December 9, 1906 - January 1, 1992) was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and United States Navy rear admiral.

Producer of Japan's first major turn-based role-playing video game, this Dutch-born American entrepreneur also secured console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game and resolved the licensing disputes that brought it to the Game Boy — who is he?
Henk Rogers is a Dutch-born American video game designer and entrepreneur.

This large insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, with more than 150,000 described species, many of whose females have an egg-laying organ often modified into a stinger — what is it called?
Hymenoptera is a large order of insects, comprising the sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants.

Also known by the old names green vitriol and copperas, this heptahydrate salt dissolves in water to form a paramagnetic, octahedral aquo complex and is used medically to fight anemia — which compound is it?
Iron(II) sulfate (British) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4xH2O.
Originally trained as a mathematician, this English economist built the foundation for an entire school of macroeconomic thought that bears his name — who is he?

John Maynard Keynes (KAYNZ; 5 June 1883 - 21 April 1946), was an English economist whose writings are considered the basis for the school of thought known as Keynesian economics, as well as its various offshoots.
Native to southern China but long cultivated in Japan and Southeast Asia, this small fruit closely resembles an orange in color and texture but is only about the size of a large olive — what is it?
Kumquat are a group of small, angiosperm, fruit-bearing trees in the family Rutaceae.

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
Raised in Wilmington, Delaware by Turkish immigrant parents, this cardiac surgeon co-founded a complementary-care center for heart patients before finding fame on television — who is he?

Mehmet Oz (mə-MET JENG-ghiz oz; born June 11, 1960), also known as Dr. Oz, is an American television presenter, physician, author, educator, and government official serving as the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) since 2025.
The dried leaves of this Southeast Asian evergreen tree, known as kratom, contain alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors as partial agonists. What plant is it?
Mitragyna speciosa is a tropical evergreen tree of the Rubiaceae family native to Southeast Asia.
This genus of spring-blooming perennials in the amaryllis family is better known by common names like daffodil and jonquil, with trumpet-shaped flowers usually white and yellow. What is it?
Narcissus (plant) is a genus of predominantly spring flowering perennial plants of the amaryllis family, Amaryllidaceae.
Also called the coypu, this plant-eating rodent digs streamside burrows and now troubles several countries as an invasive species far from its South American home — what is it?
Nutria (Myocastor coypus) is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent from South America.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This mammalian skin secretion comes in two types — a watery kind for cooling and an oilier kind found in the armpits that gains odor from bacteria — what is it?
Perspiration is the fluid secreted by sweat glands in the skin of mammals.
Its common name is shared with an unrelated tropical fruit, but this genus of roughly 200 herbaceous species — also called fleaworts — belongs to the family Plantaginaceae. Which genus?
Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.
Roaming the interior of western and central North America, this even-toed mammal survived the Pleistocene extinction of its close relatives and evolved to resemble an antelope — which creature is it?
Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.
Bitter-tasting and rich in vitamin K, this Mediterranean vegetable with edible buds resembling broccoli is also known as broccoli rabe — what is it?
Rapini (broccoli rabe or raab; RAHB) is a green cruciferous vegetable, with the leaves, buds, and stems all being edible; the buds somewhat resemble broccoli.
Operating under a pseudonym borrowed from The Princess Bride, this American created the first modern darknet marketplace before his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht (born March 27, 1984) is an American cybercriminal who created and operated Silk Road, the first modern darknet market, from 2011 until his arrest in 2013.
This American entrepreneur co-founded a pioneering file-sharing service and later became the first president of a social network that would grow into Facebook — who is he?

Sean Parker (born December 3, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and philanthropist, most notable for co-founding the file-sharing computer service Napster, and was the first president of the social networking website Facebook.
Pythons and boas of this limbless reptile group still carry a tiny pelvic girdle and vestigial leg-stubs near the cloaca, hinting at long-lost legs. What animal is this?
Snake are elongated legless reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

Known for a leather-like smell when freshly milled and prized for durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood tree bears small, fragrant white flowers and large, papery, often-hairy leaves — name this tree?
Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood tree species in the family Lamiaceae.

A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid that helps give gasoline and paint fumes their aroma, this benzene relative — a methyl group on a phenyl ring — serves as paint thinner and industrial solvent. What is it?
Toluene is a substituted aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C6H5CH3, often abbreviated as PhCH3, where Ph stands for the phenyl group.
Native to boreal forests and Arctic tundra across the Northern Hemisphere, this small evergreen heath-family shrub produces edible berries central to Nordic cuisine — what plant is it?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea is a small evergreen shrub in the heath family, Ericaceae. It is known colloquially as the lingonberry, partridgeberry, foxberry, mountain cranberry, or cowberry.
The first person to ever call himself a psychologist, this German founder of modern psychology launched Philosophische Studien, the field's first academic research journal — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt (16 August 1832 - 31 August 1920) was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology.
Also called the belly, this body region sits between the chest and pelvis and is known as the metasoma in arthropods — which body part?
Abdomen: Part of the body between the chest and pelvis. The area occupied by the abdomen is called the abdominal cavity.

Now built by Leonardo but originally developed jointly by an Italian and an American helicopter maker, this 15-seat medium twin-engine helicopter serves VIP transport, firefighting, and search-and-rescue roles — which aircraft?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
AgustaWestland AW139: Twin-engined, medium-lift helicopter manufactured by Leonardo.

Believed to be an autoimmune attack on the immune privilege of hair follicles, this condition typically leaves a few coin-sized bald spots — and in rare cases takes every hair on the body. What's it called?
Alopecia areata: Medical condition. Alopecia areata (AA), also known as spot baldness, is a condition in which hair is lost from some or all areas of the body.
Struck off the medical register for 'serious professional misconduct,' this former surgeon authored the fraudulent 1998 Lancet paper falsely tying the MMR vaccine to autism — who is he?
The average adult sheds 50 to 70 billion cells a day through this tidy, programmed cell death — named from a Greek word for 'falling off' — quite unlike messy, traumatic necrosis. What is it?
Apoptosis: Form of programmed cell death. Because apoptosis cannot stop once it has begun, it is a highly regulated process.
From the Greek for 'lack of order,' this neurological sign involves loss of voluntary muscle coordination, often linked to cerebellum dysfunction — what is it called?
Ataxia: Neurological impairment of voluntary muscle movement.
Originating in Central Africa, this hunting dog breed doesn't bark but makes an unusual yodel-like sound instead, earning it a nickname — what breed is it?
Basenji: Central African breed of dog. The Fédération Cynologique Internationale places it in the Spitz and "primitive types" categories, while the American Kennel Club classifies it as a hound.
Coined by Károly Ereky in 1919, this multidisciplinary field harnesses bacteria, yeast, and plants — often via genetic engineering — to create products and services. What field?
Biotechnology: Use of living systems and organisms to develop or make useful products.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Surprisingly, the closest living relatives of birds are a clan of semiaquatic predators that includes alligators, caimans, and the long-snouted gharial. What is this reptile order?
Crocodilia: Order of reptiles. The teeth are conical and peg-like, and the bite is powerful.
This Manhattan Project physicist later led the Federation of American Scientists and is best remembered for his 1959 Senate testimony opposing Lewis Strauss's Commerce nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill: American nuclear physicist (1919–2008)
Named for the unique double-beamed bones under its tail, this long-necked Jurassic giant is one of the most common fossils found in North America's Morrison Formation. What dinosaur is it?
Diplodocus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs (fossil)
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.

This anaerobic parasite infects tens of millions of people worldwide, causing a gut disease whose name comes from a word meaning tissue disintegration, and kills over 55,000 people each year — what is it?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Developed by IBM with a reference manual released in 1956, this programming language became the go-to choice for numerical weather prediction and supercomputer benchmarks — what language is it?
Running from mouth to anus, this passageway includes the esophagus, stomach, and intestines and handles digestion and nutrient absorption — what is it?
Gastrointestinal tract: Organ system within humans and other animals.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?
This Dutch programmer created a popular programming language and held the title 'benevolent dictator for life' until stepping down in 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum: Dutch programmer and creator of Python (born 1956)
Tapeworms, flukes and roundworms all fall under this broad name for any infection where parasitic worms take up residence in the body. What is the condition called?
Helminthiasis: Any macroparasitic disease caused by helminths.
Belonging to the genus Apis, this eusocial insect builds perennial nests of hexagonal wax cells and stores surplus food as a prized sweet — which creature is it?
This condition, caused by low blood potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, can bring on fatigue, leg cramps, and a dangerously slow heart rhythm — what is it?
Hypokalemia: Insufficient potassium in the blood. Normal potassium levels in humans are between 3.5 and 5.0 mmol/L (3.5 and 5.0 mEq/L) with levels below 3.5 mmol/L defined as hypokalemia.
Discovered by Bernard Courtois in 1811, this heaviest stable halogen melts to a deep violet liquid and is the heaviest essential nutrient — needed to make thyroid hormones. What element is it?
Iodine: Chemical element with atomic number 53 (I)
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
These paired skin folds run from the mons pubis to the perineum and are considered the anatomical counterpart to the male scrotum — what are they called?
Labia majora: Folds of skin that contain and protect the vulva's other parts.
This synthetic thyroid hormone treats hypothyroidism, has a half-life of roughly 7.5 days, and is not intended for weight loss — what's this medication?
Levothyroxine: Thyroid hormone medication. Levothyroxine, also known as L-thyroxine, is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4).
Patented in 1980 and marketed as Claritin, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever and hives but can still cause sleepiness and dry mouth — what is it?
Loratadine: Antihistamine medication. Loratadine, sold under the brand name Claritin among others, is a medication used to treat allergies.
Produced when beta-amylase breaks starch down two glucose units at a time, which reducing disaccharide gets its name from the germinating-seed process of malting?
Grown from the YF-17 that lost the Air Force's lightweight fighter contest, which twin-engine carrier jet won a second life when the Navy picked it instead?
McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet: American carrier-capable multirole strike aircraft.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem, winning both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize — who is he?
With velvety fur, tiny eyes, and powerful digging forelimbs, this subterranean mammal aerates garden soil and feasts on earthworms and slugs despite being seen as a pest — what is it?
Mole (animal): Common name for several small mammals.
This condition describes an abnormally dilated pupil that remains enlarged even in bright light, often triggered by trauma, disease, or certain drugs — what is it called?
Mydriasis: Excessive dilation of the pupil.
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the menstrual cycle, this event sees the ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg — which breaks down in under a day if it isn't fertilized. What is it called?
Ovulation: Release of egg cells from the ovaries.
This Austrian theoretical physicist, who befriended Einstein in Prague in 1912 and later hosted him often in Leiden, lent his name to a theorem and key work on phase transitions — who was he?
Found naturally in chocolate — especially after fermentation — this trace amine stimulates the central nervous system by binding to a receptor called TAAR1. What compound is it?
Phenethylamine: Organic compound, a stimulant in humans.
Native to Eurasia and temperate Africa but now naturalized worldwide, this flowering plant shares a common name with a banana-like fruit despite being unrelated to it — which species?
Plantago major: Species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.
Covering the front part of the frontal lobe, this brain region orchestrates higher-order thinking including focus, decision-making, and impulse control — what is it?
Prefrontal cortex: Part of the brain responsible for personality, decision-making, and social behavior.
Emitting beams of radiation from its magnetic poles like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star produces remarkably precise, repeating pulses — what is it?
Pulsar: Type of neutron star with beams of radiation.

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
When an infection-triggered immune overreaction sends blood pressure plummeting and disrupts cells throughout the body, doctors in the ICU are treating this life-threatening condition — what is it?
Septic shock: Dangerously low blood pressure due to damage from an organ infection.
Roughly 21 feet long yet coiled to fit inside the abdomen, this digestive tube receives bile and pancreatic juice and is divided into the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum — which organ?
